panels.title: Total value

targets.expr: sum(max by (ship, good) (spacetraders_ship_cargo_units{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"}) * on (good) group_left () avg by (good) (spacetraders_market_sell_price{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"})) or (max(spacetraders_agent_credits{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"}) * 0)

panels.description: Stacked: the top line is the total value. Ships and equipment count at what was paid for them (starting ships at 0); cargo at the average sell price over the markets seen. A purchase moves value between bands and leaves the top line about level.

panels.title: Profit per hour by activity

targets.expr: (sum by (activity) (increase(spacetraders_trip_profit_credits_total{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"}[1h])) or (sum by (activity) (increase(spacetraders_trip_loss_credits_total{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"}[1h])) * 0)) - (sum by (activity) (increase(spacetraders_trip_loss_credits_total{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"}[1h])) or (sum by (activity) (increase(spacetraders_trip_profit_credits_total{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"}[1h])) * 0))

panels.description: What each kind of work earned, booked when its trip ends: sales − purchases − fuel (trade, mining, siphoning, spare time); contracts: payments − the fuel of their trips; construction: the jump gate's materials and their fuel, always a loss, as supplying pays nothing (slice 6.6). Negative when trips lost money.

panels.title: Earned per hour, by source
panels.description: By ledger category: TradeSell, ContractDeposit, ContractPayout.

panels.title: Spent per hour, by category
panels.description: By ledger category: FuelPurchase, TradeBuy, ShipPurchase, and ConstructionBuy for the jump gate's materials (slice 6.6).

panels.title: Fleet

targets.expr: max by (ship, role, state, goal, reason) (time() - spacetraders_ship_status_since_timestamp_seconds{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"})

sum by (ship) (spacetraders_ship_cargo_units{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"}) or 0 * max by (ship) (spacetraders_ship_cargo_capacity_units{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"})

panels.description: Name: the bot's own name for the ship, beside the game's symbol (SpaceTraders slice 2.14): one name per ship type each reset, from a list per type, numbered in the order the ships joined the fleet, such as MARINER-2 for the second probe. Type: the game's registration role (EXCAVATOR for mining and siphon drones alike). Can do: what its equipment allows. Where: the waypoint and its type; while travelling, an arrow and where the ship goes. Doing: what the bot has it do: its goal in a few words, else its contract work (mining at the contract's source, delivering at its destination, on the way between them), else idle, or blocked with the reason. Arrives in: while travelling. Cargo and capacity: units in the hold and what it takes. Mined: units extracted in the dashboard's time range. Goal is the goal's kind, else the assignment (Contract), else None. Time in state counts from the bot's start at the latest.

panels.title: Roles

targets.expr: max by (ship, can) (spacetraders_ship_capabilities_info{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"}) and on (ship) max by (ship) (spacetraders_ship_role_info{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"})

max by (ship, name) (spacetraders_ship_name_info{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"}) and on (ship) max by (ship) (spacetraders_ship_role_info{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"})

panels.description: The role board (SpaceTraders slice 6.9, switch Automation.Plan.Roles.Enabled): each ship, with the bot's own name for it (slice 2.14), its role, what its equipment allows (can do), why it has the role, and what each role it could take would earn it per hour by the board's estimate (its best trip, after fuel, with the production chains' share). Why: only_role (one role whose plan is on), survey_first (it surveys, as the ship with the least to lose), contract (the contract wants ore), coverage (it keeps gathering a SCARCE or LIMITED mineral, one drone each, D48), gathers_first (a drone gathers whatever trading would pay, D58), construction (it builds the home system's jump gate: the largest hold that isn't a drone or the surveyor, D65; it trades while there is nothing it may buy), most_profitable (what earns the fleet most per hour), no_work (none of its roles had a trip; it keeps its role), no_role. A new role takes effect when the ship's trip ends. An empty cell: the ship can't take that role, or its plan is off. With the board off, the table says No data: the bot exports the roles only while the plans follow them (what each ship can do is in the fleet table). Each change is a RoleChanged line in the journal.

sum by (ship) (max by (ship, category) (spacetraders_ship_ledger_credits{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date", category=~"TradeSell|MiningSell"})) or 0 * max by (ship) (spacetraders_ship_value_credits{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"}) and on () count(spacetraders_ship_ledger_credits{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"})

sum by (ship) (max by (ship, category) (spacetraders_ship_ledger_credits{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date", category="FuelPurchase"})) or 0 * max by (ship) (spacetraders_ship_value_credits{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"}) and on () count(spacetraders_ship_ledger_credits{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"})

sum by (ship) (max by (ship, category) (spacetraders_ship_ledger_credits{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date", category!~"ShipPurchase|MountPurchase|ModulePurchase|TradeBuy|TradeSell|MiningSell|FuelPurchase"})) or 0 * max by (ship) (spacetraders_ship_value_credits{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"}) and on () count(spacetraders_ship_ledger_credits{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"})

sum by (ship) (max by (ship, category) (spacetraders_ship_ledger_credits{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"})) or 0 * max by (ship) (spacetraders_ship_value_credits{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"}) and on () count(spacetraders_ship_ledger_credits{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"})

panels.description: What each ship has made since it joined the fleet, from the bot's ledger (SpaceTraders slice 2.16), most first. profit: the sum of the columns after it, in which a cost is negative: what the ship sold, less its purchase, the cargo it bought, its fuel and its other costs. purchase: what was paid for the ship and the mounts and modules installed on it; 0 for a starting ship. market buys: the cargo it bought to trade. market sales: everything it sold, traded, mined or siphoned. fuel: its refuels. other: the rest booked to the ship: antimatter for its jumps, the jump gate's materials it bought (supplying pays nothing, so building only costs, slice 6.6) and repairs. The contract's payments are the agent's, not a ship's, so no row has them: a ship that mines and delivers for the contract shows only its fuel here (Profit per hour by activity shows the contract's). A trader between its purchase and its sale shows the purchase until it sells. The ledger keeps 30 days, longer than a reset lasts. The bottom row: the fleet's totals.

panels.title: Purchase order

targets.expr: max by (position, tier, plan, ship_type, shipyard) (spacetraders_purchase_need_credits{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"})

max by (position, tier, plan, ship_type, shipyard) (spacetraders_purchase_need_credits{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"}) + on () group_left () max(spacetraders_credit_reserve{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"})

panels.description: The order ships are bought in (SpaceTraders slice 6.10b, D43): what each plan that buys ships would buy now. The lowest position is first in line: the credits are saved up for it, and the purchases after it wait until it is bought or no longer needed (the ships still work). 1 Contract: the contract's drone. 2 Surveyor: a designated surveyor (D47). 3 Coverage: a drone per SCARCE or LIMITED mineral and area (D48, D53). 4 SurveyorPerArea: one more surveyor per area with mining drones (D55). 5 CargoShips: the next ship of Trade.ShipPurchases, saved up for. 6 Construction: the jump gate's next load of materials (D64), with the material as the ship type and its market as the shipyard; while the gate needs materials, what comes after waits. The Mining plan's SHIP_MINING_DRONE at this position is one of the gate's miners (slice 6.25, D92): one per ore every Mining.GateMinerIntervalMinutes (30) while a smelter that makes a metal for the gate's materials from the ore has it below HIGH. It waits while a load can be bought, and is bought while the load waits for SCARCE or LIMITED markets. 7 Explorer: the first explorer (slice 6.30, D98); a probe of ours in the shipyard's system, or on its way there, answers the purchase's call, else the command ship fetches it (slice 6.32, D108). 8 Probes: a probe per market (D29) of home and of the explored systems within the trade reach, Trade.MaxHaulDistance jumps of home (slice 6.28, D97); the shipyards first, those that sell SHIP_EXPLORER first of all, wherever the gates reach them (slice 6.32, D109, D111). 9 Alternating: drones and cargo ships in turn. 10 MoreExplorers: every further explorer (D102: one for every Explore.SystemsPerExplorer systems left to explore, at most Explore.MaxExplorers); a probe of ours answers the purchase's call, else the command ship fetches it (slice 6.32, D108). 11 FarProbes: a probe per market of the other explored systems, last (D97), the shipyards first (slice 6.32, D109); the shipyard can be one abroad, where a probe of ours is. credits needed is the price and the reserve a purchase leaves (D51). A plan that needs nothing has no row; No data: nothing to buy.

panels.title: Jump gate progress
panels.description: How much of its materials the home system's jump gate has, by us or anyone: all units supplied over all units it needs (slice 6.6). It opens the gate network once complete. No data until the construction plan has seen the gate under construction (Automation.Plan.Construction.Enabled).

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (site) (max by (site, trade_symbol) (spacetraders_construction_units_fulfilled{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"})) / sum by (site) (max by (site, trade_symbol) (spacetraders_construction_units_required{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"}))

panels.title: Jump gate: materials still needed
panels.description: The materials the home system's jump gate still needs: what is left to supply, what it has, and what it needs in all. A material it has all of drops off the table. The construction role's ship buys them a full hold at a time, where the market isn't SCARCE or LIMITED (D64-D67).

targets.expr: max by (site, trade_symbol) (spacetraders_construction_units_required{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"}) - max by (site, trade_symbol) (spacetraders_construction_units_fulfilled{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"})

panels.title: Jump gate materials
panels.description: Each material of the home system's jump gate: the share of what it needs that it has.

targets.expr: 100 * max by (site, trade_symbol) (spacetraders_construction_units_fulfilled{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"}) / max by (site, trade_symbol) (spacetraders_construction_units_required{namespace="spacetraders", reset_date=~"$reset_date"})

panels.title: API request rates
panels.description: Requests to the game API per second, over 5 minutes. Initiated: each request the bot starts, counted once, before it waits for the bot's budget (2 a second plus a burst of 30 a minute) and before the pause after a 502. Executed: each request that went out, retries of a 429 included. Completed: each one that got an answer, whatever its status. Rate limited: the answers that were a 429. Initiated above executed: requests wait for the budget, or the pause refuses them; executed above initiated: retries. Initiated needs the bot's slice 2.10.

panels.title: API requests per minute, by endpoint
panels.description: Every attempt, retries included. The limit is 2 a second plus a burst of 30 a minute.

panels.title: 429s, failed calls and rate-limit waits
panels.description: Per 5 minutes. A 429 from the rate limiter means the bot's budget let too much through (D3).

panels.title: Messages per minute, by type
panels.description: A loop shows up here first.

panels.title: Goal steps per minute, and circuit breaker trips
panels.description: The tick alone takes 12 steps a minute per busy ship; the breaker blocks a goal above 60.

panels.title: Database size
panels.description: The lines are the default soft (1 GiB) and hard (3 GiB) limits.

panels.title: Active anomalies
panels.description: Until phase 3 only the database size limits raise anomalies; the journal below says when each was raised.

panels.title: Settings

targets.expr: label_replace(max by (setting, current, next_run, description) (spacetraders_setting_info{namespace="spacetraders", setting!~"Runtime[.].*", current=~"true|false", reset_date=~"$reset_date"}), "order", "1 $1", "setting", "(.*)") or label_replace(max by (setting, current, next_run, description) (spacetraders_setting_info{namespace="spacetraders", setting!~"Runtime[.].*", current!~"true|false", reset_date=~"$reset_date"}), "order", "2 $1", "setting", "(.*)")

panels.description: Every setting the bot has, with its value now, the value the next run starts with, and what it does. The switches (true or false) come first, on in green; then the other settings by name. A value that may hold a secret shows (hidden), as in the journal. Left out: the Runtime.* status flags, which aren't settings to tune. What a setting does is what the running version says. The next run is the agent the next server reset registers: it starts with the value chosen for it, else the default. PUT /settings/{key} changes a setting now and for the next runs; PUT /settings/next-run/{key} only for the next runs, and DELETE /settings/next-run/{key} gives them the default again (the bot's own dashboard only shows settings). The blue "Setting changes" annotations mark when each changed. The bot samples its settings every 10 seconds, and Prometheus scrapes it every minute.

panels.title: Log lines per hour

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({namespace="spacetraders"} | json ResetDate | drop __error__, __error_details__ | ResetDate=~"$reset_date" or ResetDate="" [1h]))

panels.description: Budget: 5,000 lines a day per ship, the dashed line (about 208 an hour a ship). The alert compares the last 24 hours with the ships averaged over them. Loki's 31 days on 10Gi are shared with every app.

panels.title: Journal

targets.expr: {namespace="spacetraders"} | json EventKind, ResetDate, ShipName, message="[\"@m\"]" | EventKind != "" | ResetDate=~"$reset_date" | line_format "{{ if .ShipName }}[{{ .ShipName }}] {{ end }}{{ .message }}"

panels.description: One line per meaningful thing (JournalEvents): contracts, purchases and sales, plans, idle and blocked ships, setting changes, resets and anomalies. Open a line for its properties. A line about a ship starts with the bot's own name for it, in brackets (slice 2.14).

panels.title: Errors

targets.expr: {namespace="spacetraders"} |~ `"@l":"(?:Error|Fatal)"|^[^{].*(?i:error)` | json message="[\"@m\"]", ResetDate | ResetDate=~"$reset_date" or ResetDate="" | line_format `{{ if .message }}{{ .message }}{{ else }}{{ __line__ }}{{ end }}`

panels.description: What the "SpaceTraders logged errors" alert counts: the bot's lines at level Error or Fatal, and lines from nginx or the init container containing "error". Warnings that repeat raise the RepeatingError anomaly instead. Open a line for its properties.

list.name: reset_date
list.label: Reset
list.description: The server reset whose run the dashboard shows, newest first (slice 2.13): every series carries it as reset_date and every log line as ResetDate, so runs never mix. Tick several to compare runs. Data from before slice 2.13 has no reset date and shows under none.
